A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cluster-DAG causal-discovery work. Their complete text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and expanded experiments.

before.justification: v2 reports four original simulation studies comparing Cluster-PC and Cluster-FCI with baseline algorithms, including numerical results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 reports expanded original simulations and a new bootstrapped evaluation on the Sachs protein-signaling dataset in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same graph initialization, conditional-independence testing, and orientation procedures. The non-PAG Cluster-FCI variant also already appears in v2. The new k-PC discussion introduces a comparator, not a modification to the proposed methods.

E1.justification: v3 extends the previously simulation-only evaluation to the Sachs protein-signaling dataset, whose reference graph contains a cycle. Simulation 2 also adds Logistic and MIM data-generation cases. The other application domains discussed in Appendix E are motivational examples, not additional evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: v3 adds k-PC with k=2 to Simulation 1's PC versus Cluster-PC comparison and includes it in the new Sachs evaluation. Simulation 2 retains PC versus Cluster-PC, and the FCI studies retain their existing FCI, Cluster-FCI, and FCITiers membership.

E3.justification: The reported grids expand substantially: v2 Table 3 specifies one node count per study and 1,000 samples, whereas v3 Table 4 varies node counts and uses 300, 1,000, and 3,000 samples. Edge-count settings also change, and Simulation 2 replaces its significance-level sweep with alpha=0.05. Appendix F introduces a Sachs protocol using Fisher-z at alpha=0.01.

E4.justification: New Figure 4 explicitly examines sensitivity to graph size and sample size. The existing distribution-sensitivity analysis gains Logistic and MIM cases in Table 6. These extend the earlier robustness analyses; no new method-component ablation is introduced.

E5.justification: v2 reports run counts but presents point estimates without uncertainty intervals. v3 introduces 95% t-based confidence intervals in Figures 3–5 and Table 1, plus uncertainty entries in other result tables. Reported runs per configuration increase from 5 to 20 for Simulation 4, and Appendix F adds 100 bootstrap resamples.

E6.justification: Simulation results are substantially replaced under revised settings, so their numerical differences are not same-setting performance changes. For Simulation 3, C-FCI/FCITiers arrow precision changes from 29.9%/29.8% in v2 Table 2 to 24.1%/25.2% in v3 Table 2, reversing their ordering. New k-PC and Sachs results are added; Sachs SHD is 21.5 for Cluster-PC, 22.9 for PC, and 30.9 for k-PC.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, Theorems 1–7, Appendix A proofs, Appendix C pairwise characterizations, and Appendix D optimization formulation remain unchanged apart from formatting and references. The Sachs experiment does not introduce a theoretical relaxation of the DAG assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims about C-DAG expressiveness, the two algorithms, their soundness/completeness properties, and empirical advantages. The additional examples and experiments support these retained contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v3 explains the accuracy versus test-count tradeoff with k-PC and adds application arguments in Appendix E. Revised FCI table captions emphasize similar performance with fewer tests. The earlier assertion that lower alpha can largely remove Cluster-PC's precision disadvantage is dropped, while the existing C-FCI incompleteness discussion remains.

D1.justification: v3 newly identifies gCastle for simulation generation and causal-discovery-toolbox as the Sachs data source. Appendix F specifies its testing settings and depicts the assumed cluster graph. These improve implementation documentation; the code-access statement still identifies the same repository.

R1.justification: v3 adds an explicit comparison with Kocaoglu's k-PC and literature supporting applications in biology, climate, health, and macroeconomics. It also adds dataset/software citations and removes the Li et al. (2024) representation-learning discussion. The central positioning against tiered background knowledge and causal-abstraction research remains.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v3 adds related-work subheadings, short explanatory passages, Appendices E–F, and publication/review header text, while removing the acknowledgment. Some duplicated wording is introduced in Section 3.1.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially reorganized: Figure 3 gains k-PC and error bars, new Figure 4 presents sensitivity plots, and the earlier Figure 4 becomes a revised Figure 5. Combined simulation tables are separated, appendix tables align comparator columns and add arrow metrics, and Sachs graph figures and a result table are added. The document is also retypeset.

improvement.justification: The k-PC comparison, uncertainty intervals, and broader sensitivity analyses make v3's empirical evidence more informative. Sachs adds useful mixed results, although its cyclic reference limits interpretation under the DAG assumptions. The gain is tempered by unreconciled reporting: retained prose claims better C-FCI arrow precision than FCITiers, while revised Table 2 reports 24.1% versus 25.2%.
